name: OR-04
label: Likely D

key_factors: Incumbent Val Hoyle runs in a district that leans Democratic by six points, and the fundamentals favor her
Prediction markets price Hoyle at about a 95% chance of winning
No public general-election polling exists, keeping uncertainty elevated
DeSpain has raised $678K to Hoyle's $1.2M, with only modest outside spending on either side
model.rationale: Hoyle's incumbency and the district's Democratic lean give her a clear edge, and prediction markets price her near 95% to win. With no public polling and only modest outside spending behind DeSpain, the race looks firmly Democratic, though the absence of survey data argues against calling it safe.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for DeSpain or her first public polling showing a single-digit race would signal a genuine contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oregon's 4th District leans Democratic by about six points on the partisan index, and incumbent Val Hoyle is seeking re-election. Her Republican challenger, Monique DeSpain, has raised roughly $678,000 — a respectable sum but well short of Hoyle's $1.2 million. Outside groups have put modest money into the race on both sides, about $300,000 opposing Hoyle and a similar amount supporting her.

No public general-election polls are available, and no race raters have published ratings for the contest. Prediction markets nonetheless price Hoyle around a 95% chance of winning, reflecting her incumbency and the district's lean. A third-party candidate, Justin Filip, appears on the ballot but is not viewed as a factor. The seat remains on the Democratic side of the ledger, with the main open question being the size of Hoyle's winning margin.
